To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fire behaviour is influenced by the adhesive and that the fire resistance is lower for CLT than for homogeneous timber panels of the same thickness.
the fire behaviour and charring of cross laminated timbers is highly dependent on the adhesive properties.
the fire behaviour (charring) of cross laminated panels in fire is strongly influenced by: (1) the adhesive used for gluing the layers together; and (2) the moisture content of the panels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed analysis of the fire behaviour and the fire resistance of cross laminated wood panels.
the fire behaviour of timber members and structures.
the development of design models for the fire behaviour of timber structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cross laminated timber is not more fire resistant than homogeneous timber.
for cross laminated timber the fire behaviour is strongly influenced by both the adhesive as well as the type of the timber used for the cross laminated panels.
the fire behaviour is influenced by the behaviour and properties of the adhesive at elevated temperatures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fire behaviour in the fire tests was not only influenced by the charring of the timber layers but also by the behaviour of adhesives at high temperature.
the charring rate of cross laminated panels can be estimated with the charring rates for homogeneous timber members.
for fire design of CLT panels the charring rate should be taken into account, but the falling off of the chared layer has to be considered as well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the charring of CLT panels is not necessarily different than that of homogeneous timber members.
cross laminated timber panel fire design needs to take into account the behaviour of the adhesively bonded cross laminated timber in fire.
the fire resistance of cross laminated panels is not only determined by the fire properties of the individual wood layers but also by the adhesive used for the bonding of the wood layers.
